title: Fix the Missing Address-Of Operator
description: The program should read an integer from the user and print it.
expectedBehavior: The program should read the typed number into age and print it back.
actualProblem: scanf needs the memory address of age to store the input into, but age (without &) passes its current (uninitialized) value instead of its address. scanf then tries to write to that garbage 'address', which is undefined behavior and usually crashes.
expectedOutput: Enter your age: You are 25 years old
explanation: scanf() writes its result directly into memory, so it needs a pointer (an address) to know where to write. The & (address-of) operator supplies that address; forgetting it is one of the most common C beginner mistakes.
